newsitem.title: UK: Imperial Tobacco says outlook as forecast.
newsitem.headline: Imperial Tobacco says outlook as forecast.

text.p: Imperial Tobacco, in its first set of financial results since it was spun off from Hanson Plc last October, said on Wednesday its business outlook for the rest of the year was in line with its expectations.

The company, which owns the John Player Special and Embassy brands, announced profits before tax of 143 million pounds in the six months ended March 29, 1997 against brokers forecast range of 136 to 150 million pounds.

But looking longer term, chairman Derek Bonham said, "Against the background of a gradually declining UK market, the development of our international business remains fundamental to our future strategy."
Imperial's share of the British cigarette market grew to 38.4 percent from 37.9 percent, but the market showed signs of decline over the period.

Former Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's November budget pushed premium cigarette brand prices through 3.0 pounds ($4.89) per pack, turning many smokers to take up cheaper brands. Imperial's Lambert & Butler brands in the low price sector continued to sell well, accounting for 12 percent of the British market.
Britian's cigarette market has fallen some three percent since the Budget with Imperial selling just under 15 billion sticks since November. About 80 billion cigarettes are sold each year in Britain.

However, Imperial's profits from Britain rose five million to 147 million pounds in the six month period while profits from the groups overseas business grew 13 percent to 36 million, comprising 20 percent of total group profit.
Imperial incurred a 40 million interest charge in the period from servicing 1.1 billion pounds of debt it inherited from Hanson as a result of its demerger.
Dutch cigarette paper producer Rizla International BV, which Imperial acquired for 185 million in January, contributed 4.0 million pounds to group profits. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
